podcast.body: The album *Madvillainy* by Madlib and MF Doom (Madvillain) is highlighted for its use of manual sampling processes, which resonated with the older, artisanal techniques of hip hop pioneers. This stylistic choice evoked the raw, hand-crafted sound found in records by artists like Cut Chemist, DJ Shadow, and J Dilla. "una de las cosas que yo creo que hacía interés antísimo el disco de Madlib y de MFN, el Madbillain, es que precisamente Madlib estaba usando procesos manuales de Sample como se hacía antiguamente y te recordaba los discos de Catkemi's, a los de DJ's a Do, a los de DJ's a Do, a los de J.D. La, te recordaba todos estos discos donde todo el proceso de Sample y de Artesania pura."

podcast.body: The album Madvillainy is so musically significant that it features its own instrumental version, showcasing the strength of Madlib's production independently of MF Doom's vocals. Even within the final version of the album, there are many instrumental parts that stand out and are considered excellent on their own. "el disco Mad Villani está importante que tiene su versión instrumental sin las canciones de Merdum solo en la parte instrumental porque incluso solo instrumentalmente se discos son referentes."

podcast.body: This album, a supergroup project between MF Doom and Madlib under the name Madvillain, was released in 2004. It is considered essential listening, a piece of music history, and something unique that leaves the hip hop world speechless. The album's creation involved MF Doom and Madlib working remotely before they had ever met, driven by mutual professional respect. It flowed rapidly during its initial development but was leaked online when almost finished, spreading virally and becoming a cult classic before its official release. The frustration from the leak led them to abandon the project for over a year and a half before finally reuniting to complete and release it, cementing its status as a foundational hip hop record, comparable in impact to the debut albums of Nas or Wu-Tang Clan. "Este disco sí que vale la pena para todo el mundo, es historia de la música."
